scoring: Theorem impact follows the user conditional correctness/novelty/publication rubric for the principal output emphasized in the final paper. Added contribution separately assesses this paper relative to acknowledged prior inputs; it does not re-award the upstream breakthrough. Neither score is a correctness probability. Approximate calibration uncertainty is half a point to one point.

papers.title: Signed impulse estimates and global smooth solutions for finite multispecies relativistic Vlasov-Maxwell
papers.lay_summary: For the stated smooth initial data, a relativistic collisionless plasma with finitely many kinds of charged particles evolves forever without a finite-time singularity, even for large data.
papers.importance_and_attribution: A central global-regularity conclusion in kinetic theory. This paper substantively extends the upstream one-species mechanism to distinct positive masses and arbitrary signed charges through a joint bootstrap. No infinite-species, massless or long-time scattering theorem is asserted.

papers.title: Binary consequences of relation-liveness automata lower bounds
papers.lay_summary: Some small guessing machines reading binary strings require superpolynomially larger deterministic machines, even if those machines can scan backward. Recognizing the full complement can also be vastly harder.
papers.importance_and_attribution: The conclusion settles a central automata-simulation barrier. This note adds precise binary encoding, state counts and boundary conventions; the exponential lower-bound engines and coding framework are inherited.

papers.title: Rational-point undecidability for smooth projective varieties over the rational numbers
papers.lay_summary: No algorithm can always decide whether an arbitrary smooth projective variety over the rationals has a rational point. No computable universal bound can tell us how far to search for one.
papers.importance_and_attribution: Central arithmetic/logic impossibility conclusion, effectively equivalent to rational Hilbert’s tenth problem. The geometric transfer is Poonen’s and the main arithmetic input is upstream; this package adds precise scope and two documented arithmetic corrections. Dimension and all size parameters may vary.

papers.title: Nonnegative binary rational hafnians: an exact reduction and approximation and sampling consequences
papers.lay_summary: Efficiently approximates weighted perfect-matching totals and approximately samples weighted matchings for nonnegative rational weights.
papers.importance_and_attribution: The conclusion contains the longstanding general-graph perfect-matching approximation target. This paper’s weighted reduction and counting-to-sampling mechanisms are classical; the FPRAS engine is upstream. No signed/complex hafnian or general boson-sampling theorem.

papers.title: L2-acyclicity and cost for a rank-100 amalgam
papers.lay_summary: A random group action needs more connections than its homological complexity predicts; the paper also directly checks that all of the example group’s L²-homology vanishes.
papers.importance_and_attribution: Major measured-group-theory counterexample at the relation level. The group and cost gap are upstream; this paper adds a concrete cost-independent acyclicity proof. It does not disprove equality for group-infimum cost.

papers.title: A priori estimates across the subcritical Lane–Emden hyperbola
papers.lay_summary: Two mutually coupled nonlinear elliptic equations cannot develop arbitrarily large spikes in the full strictly subcritical range. Their size is controlled by distance to the boundary.
papers.importance_and_attribution: Major full-range estimate package, closely equivalent in content to the underlying nonexistence theorem. Its new range comes from upstream; the Liouville-to-estimate and boundary reductions are established machinery. No critical or supercritical extension.

papers.title: Pure-loss bosonic dynamic capacities: EPnI consequences and consumed-key secrecy accounting
papers.lay_summary: Determines optimal tradeoffs among ordinary information, quantum information, entanglement and secrets in an ideal lossy light channel. It also finds and repairs a secrecy rule that incorrectly excludes the one-time pad.
papers.importance_and_attribution: Major quantum-information consequence of the new entropy inequality. The paper adds a genuine operational correction, counterexample and repaired coding/converse account. Private formulas hold only under its explicit replacement secrecy convention; transmissivity is at least one half and the budget is average photon number.

papers.title: Exact semidefinite complexity of the symmetric traveling-salesman polytope
papers.lay_summary: Even allowing auxiliary variables, any exact positive-semidefinite-matrix description of all traveling-salesman tours must have size exponential in the number of cities.
papers.importance_and_attribution: Major sharp quantitative advance in extension complexity. The hard matching lower bound is upstream; the note supplies an explicit refined transfer and size accounting. Older bounds already ruled out polynomial exact SDP size. No approximate-SDP or P-versus-NP conclusion.

papers.title: Bilinear ergodic Hilbert variation for commuting transformations as a consequence of annular triangular variation
papers.lay_summary: A signed, harmonic-weighted combination of two observables along commuting dynamics converges almost everywhere, with a quantitative bound on its oscillation.
papers.importance_and_attribution: Major specialized ergodic consequence. The note gives careful restriction and transference from the new triangular variation theorem. It covers L³ inputs and variation exponent greater than two; it does not solve commuting Cesàro convergence.

papers.title: Hypersingular Riesz-energy constants on surfaces from triangular-lattice universal optimality
papers.lay_summary: Determines the exact leading energy of many strongly repelling points spread over a smooth surface; the constant comes from the triangular lattice.
papers.importance_and_attribution: Major potential-theory conclusion. The paper applies established lattice-to-surface reductions to the new universal-optimality input; it does not establish local crystallization.

papers.title: Even Minkowski uniqueness as a consequence of logarithmic Brunn–Minkowski
papers.lay_summary: Shows that a prescribed symmetric curvature-type measurement determines one origin-symmetric convex shape in the stated smooth setting, across the logarithmic and related parameter range.
papers.importance_and_attribution: Important convex-geometry uniqueness theorem, obtained through published implications of the new logarithmic Brunn–Minkowski result. Smooth positive even data are essential for the logarithmic endpoint; arbitrary singular endpoint data are not covered.

papers.title: An explicit complex polynomial retract in five variables: a consequence of affine-space cancellation failure
papers.lay_summary: Constructs a polynomial projection whose image is a smooth affine variety that is not ordinary affine space.
papers.importance_and_attribution: An important negative example for affine algebraic geometry. The retract mechanism is classical and the decisive exotic variety comes from the new cancellation counterexample. The construction uses five ambient variables; the four-variable case is not settled.

papers.title: Rational Hodge classes on mixed products of K3 moduli spaces
papers.short_title: Hodge classes on K3 moduli products
papers.lay_summary: Certain cohomological features of products of K3-related moduli spaces are represented by actual algebraic geometric pieces, in every codimension.
papers.importance_and_attribution: Major specialized Hodge conclusion. The paper combines the upstream mixed-K3 result with established motivic reductions. It does not solve the general Hodge conjecture or cover arbitrary deformations, singular moduli spaces or integral classes.

papers.title: Reduced C*-algebras of the Thompson family: an attributed consequence of nonamenability
papers.lay_summary: The operator algebras built from four famous Thompson-related groups have no nontrivial proper closed ideals and admit only one normalized trace.
papers.importance_and_attribution: Important classical test cases, unlocked by F nonamenability. The needed simplicity and trace implications were already published; this is an attributed consequence note, not an independent nonamenability proof.

papers.title: Two consequences of group-algebra and planar Fourier certificates: wreath products and triangle bounds
papers.lay_summary: Combining two groups that each resist collapse can produce a group that does not. Separately, two Fourier optimization programs have the same sharp planar packing bound after normalization.
papers.importance_and_attribution: Meaningful specialist answers in two unrelated areas. Both use known transfer mechanisms and imported certificates. The packing part is planar only, and supplies neither an all-dimensional theorem nor a triangle optimizer.

papers.title: The Sperner property of standard graded Artinian complete intersections in characteristic zero
papers.lay_summary: For a broad class of finite polynomial algebras, the maximum number of generators needed by any ideal is exactly the size of the largest degree layer.
papers.importance_and_attribution: Strong specialist algebraic conclusion. The published EGH-to-Sperner implication and scope reductions already exist; the note records the newly available consequence. No weak or strong Lefschetz theorem is supplied.

papers.title: Output-sensitive sparse factorization over finite fields from dense factorization
papers.lay_summary: Factors extremely sparse polynomials without expanding their potentially enormous degrees, provided the distinct output factors themselves have manageable total degree.
papers.importance_and_attribution: Strong specialist algorithmic contribution: a new sparse-numerator/dense-denominator descent invariant handles binary exponents and multiplicities. The runtime is output-degree sensitive. General dense deterministic factorization is inherited and is not what receives this score.

papers.title: Metric rigidity at the boundary of cubic compactifications
papers.lay_summary: For the covered singular geometric spaces, the metric determines the complex geometry up to conjugation; the statement reaches the boundary of cubic compactifications.
papers.importance_and_attribution: Solid added singular high-index rigidity work and a metric-fiber consequence. The broader complex K-moduli/GIT comparison was already available in stronger form; score the actual rigidity extension rather than the abandoned first-identification ambition.

papers.title: A sharp dyadic threshold in a characteristic-two random-cone construction
papers.lay_summary: Proves the smallest dyadic permitted parameter for one group-ring counterexample recipe, reducing the construction from projective-plane order 128 to 32 and a 532-edge rose.
papers.importance_and_attribution: Useful but narrow exact calibration of a fixed construction. The dramatic characteristic-two idempotent counterexample is inherited and previously disclosed. This score concerns the new threshold, not a fresh Kaplansky solution or global generator optimality.
